title: Specialized Databases
summary: Beyond relational: graph DBs (Neo4j) excel at relationship queries (friend-of-friend, fraud rings); time-series DBs (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB)
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Beyond relational: graph DBs (Neo4j) excel at relationship queries (friend-of-friend, fraud rings); time-series DBs (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB) optimize timestamped metrics; search engines (Elasticsearch) do full-text and fuzzy matching.
Polyglot persistence means choosing per use-case: Postgres for users/orders, Elasticsearch for product search, Redis for sessions/cache.
Key points: each tool optimizes a query shape relational DBs handle poorly, and "one database for everything" is usually a compromise.

sections.codeExample:
-- graph: friends of friends
MATCH (a:Person {name:"Ada"})-[:KNOWS]->(b)-[:KNOWS]->(c)
RETURN c.name
